title: Defense giant Rheinmetall embraces ‘new normal’ of caution after military contract setback; stock rises
html:
Shares of Rheinmetall rose on Friday as investors assessed the defense giant's cautious forecasting approach at its Capital Markets Day.

It follows several recent setbacks for the German arms maker, most notably the cancellation of a major contract to build F126 warships for the country's military.

Rheinmetall now expects sales of between 33 and 37 billion euros (between $36.2 billion and $40.6 billion) by 2030, down from a previous forecast of about 45 billion euros. That guidance incorporates a "more prudent approach" for its vehicle systems business as well as its weapons and ammunition unit, now adjusted for new capacities and project delays.

Shares rose 3.4% in mid-morning trading amid a European defense sector firmly in the green.

"The opportunity has not changed; the way we plan for it has," Rheinmetall said in a company presentation.

"We are becoming more cautious whilst retaining our agility in a dynamic market," it said, highlighting a "new normal level of conservatism and recalibrated ambition" in the mid-term.

summary: The German arms maker vows a "more prudent approch" to forecast sales of tanks and ammunition.
